column1: ## The keyboard encoder's table: what each key sends, in each mode a program can ask for.
## copied into place by `scripts/dev/generate-key-encoding-table.ps1`) and of the test that runs every
## version is §4.4 of `docs/plans/design/keyboard-protocol-2026-09-29.md`; from T-KEYBOARD-PROTOCOL on,
## this file is the source and the note is history. A ticket that changes a byte changes its row here in
## the same commit. `input::tests::the_protocols_normative_cases` holds the cases the specifications
## themselves state as literals beside it, so a wrong row here cannot agree with itself.
##             or the character a US layout's key produces with no modifier (`e`, `[`, `1`)
##   location  `standard`, or `numpad` for a keypad key (winit's `KeyLocation::Numpad`)
##   mods      `-`, or any of S (Shift), A (Alt), C (Ctrl), in that order
##             `records` (on Windows, no program asked and ConPTY has win32-input-mode set: the chords
##             VT cannot express are win32-input-mode key records `CSI Vk;Sc;Uc;Kd;Cs;Rc _`, down then
##             up — T-KEYBOARD-RECORDS; every other chord is its legacy bytes)
##   bytes     `CSI ` stands for ESC [; `\e` ESC, `\r` CR, `\t` HT, `\xNN` one byte; `—` sends
##             nothing; `(table)` is a chord Folio's shortcut table claims on Windows, so the
##   note      `system` — taken by Windows before Folio sees it; `n/a` — never arrives on
##             Windows (still encoded, for macOS); otherwise empty
## A chord is built as winit hands it over on Windows with a US layout: the logical key carries
## Shift and not Ctrl (`Ctrl+Shift+1` is `!`), and the key without modifiers is the unshifted one.
## A record's character is what that layout types for the chord (`\n` for Ctrl+Enter, nothing — 0 —
## for Ctrl+1 or Ctrl+Shift+Enter), measured with `ToUnicodeEx` against the US layout.
